name: Scrub Typhus

pathogens.why: Orientia tsutsugamushi is the sole cause of scrub typhus; the clinical diagnosis (eschar, lymphadenopathy, exposure history in an endemic rural/peri-urban setting) is often sufficiently characteristic to justify empiric treatment before serology returns.

investigations.why: Eschar (a painless, often overlooked necrotic lesion at the chigger bite site) is highly specific for scrub typhus when found — actively look in skin folds, axillae, groin.

investigations.test: Scrub typhus IgM ELISA / Weil-Felix (less specific)
investigations.why: Confirms diagnosis serologically, though treatment should not wait for results when clinical suspicion is high.
Assesses organ involvement; transaminitis and thrombocytopenia are common supportive findings.
Screens for ARDS, a recognized complication of severe/delayed scrub typhus.

references: NCDC India Guidelines for Rickettsial Diseases
reasonSource: e=>`Fever with ${e.eschar?"a pathognomonic eschar":"lymphadenopathy and/or rural/scrub vegetation exposure"} is consistent with scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi infection) — a rickettsial illness that is readily treatable with antibiotics but can progress to multi-organ dysfunction (ARDS, myocarditis, encephalitis) if treatment is delayed. Empiric doxycycline should be started promptly on clinical suspicion without waiting for serology confirmation, given the excellent response to early treatment and the risk of severe disease with delay.`
